title: Unramified universally injective space morphisms are representable by schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and point spaces [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume $f$ is unramified: its chart test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] is the scheme unramified property [def-weil-unramified-morphism], including local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $f$ is universally injective: for every algebraic-space morphism $Y'\to Y$, the map $|X\times_Y Y'|\to|Y'|$ is injective. Then $f$ is representable by schemes: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to Y$, the sheaf $X\times_Y h_T$ is represented by a scheme.

source.place: Tag 05W6 (spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-universally-injective-unramified), moreover clause under condition (2), representability assertion only.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and a map $h_T\to Y$. Regard $h_T$ as an algebraic space and put $E=X\times_Yh_T$, with projection $g:E\to h_T$. The fibre-product result makes $E$ an algebraic space. By base-change permanence, $g$ is unramified, hence locally of finite type on etale scheme charts. No representability of $g$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 05W6, lemma-universally-injective-unramified, proof of (2) implies (1) and the moreover clause; first base change to an arbitrary scheme test.

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is universally injective directly from the hypothesis: for every $B\to h_T$, associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies $E\times_{h_T}B$ with $X\times_YB$, preserving the projection to $B$. In particular the first projection $p:E\times_{h_T}E\to E$ is injective on point classes. Write $\delta:E\to E\times_{h_T}E$ for the diagonal. Since $p\delta=1_E$, for any point $z$ of $E\times_{h_T}E$ we have $p(\delta(p(z)))=p(z)$; injectivity gives $\delta(p(z))=z$. Thus $|\delta|$ is surjective. These identifications follow sectionwise from the compatible-pair definition of the fibre product.

source.place: Tag 05W6, lemma-universally-injective-unramified, proof of (2) implies (1) and the moreover clause; first base change to an arbitrary scheme test.

proof.text: Apply the open-diagonal theorem to the unramified morphism $g$ with scheme target $T$: $\delta$ is a representable open immersion. Its point image is all of $|E\times_{h_T}E|$ by the preceding step. The open-subspace criterion therefore identifies this open subspace with the whole target, so $\delta$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $g$ is a monomorphism of sheaves: for every test scheme $H$, any pair $e_1,e_2\in E(H)$ with equal image in $h_T(H)$ is a section of $E\times_{h_T}E$; the inverse of $\delta$ expresses it as $(e,e)$, giving $e_1=e_2$.

source.place: Tag 05W6, lemma-universally-injective-unramified, proof of (2) implies (1) and the moreover clause; first base change to an arbitrary scheme test.

proof.text: The locally-finite-type monomorphism theorem now applies to $g:E\to h_T$: the chartwise local finite type was obtained in step 1 and injectivity on sections in step 3. It gives separatedness and chartwise local quasi-finiteness, with no quasi-compactness assumption.

source.place: Tag 05W6, lemma-universally-injective-unramified, proof of (2) implies (1) and the moreover clause; first base change to an arbitrary scheme test.

proof.text: Apply the separated locally quasi-finite space-over-a-scheme theorem to $E\to T$. Its two hypotheses are precisely the conclusions of step 4. It supplies a scheme $Z$ over $T$ and an isomorphism $h_Z\simeq E$ over $h_T$. Since the scheme $T$ and its map to $Y$ were arbitrary, every sheaf $X\times_Yh_T$ is represented by a scheme, which is the required representability of $f$.

source.place: Tag 05W6, lemma-universally-injective-unramified, proof of (2) implies (1) and the moreover clause; first base change to an arbitrary scheme test.

The item statement is unchanged from live, which is still unsplit, and there is no repair note, so this is a first split of an empty proof. The five steps follow Stacks' route after base-changing to an arbitrary S-scheme T. Step 1: def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, the fibre-products node and unramified permanence give an unramified, locally finite type E -> h_T. Step 2 is elementary and correct: universal injectivity passes to g by associativity of fibre products; p is injective on points and p.delta = 1, so |delta| is surjective. Step 3: lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal makes delta a representable open immersion; lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus says an open subspace with full point image is the whole space, so delta is an isomorphism and g is a monomorphism, written out with compatible pairs. Step 4: the hypotheses of lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf (monomorphism into h_T, locally finite type on charts) are met; it gives separated and locally quasi-finite. Step 5: lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable (03XX) has exactly those hypotheses and gives h_Z = E. No new nodes; the DAG search for 05W6/040X/0418/0463/03XX/05W1 found no duplicate. Small cases checked: empty X or T, open immersion, purely inseparable extension excluded, non-quasi-compact T. No SGA. The three declared generic tool_uses (fibre products, point-open calculus, 03XX) are accepted.
